lesson.title: Build a REST API with FastAPI
lesson.goal: build a REST API with FastAPI: GET and POST endpoints with Pydantic models, run with uvicorn

sources.title: Build a REST API with FastAPI

steps.title: Install packages and create root endpoint
steps.instructions: In a new project directory, run pip install fastapi uvicorn, then create main.py with a FastAPI app instance. Add a root GET route that returns a Hello World dictionary.

targets.caption: Define the root GET route in main.py

explanations.topic: Using @app.get decorator to define root path

hints: Make sure both fastapi and uvicorn are installed in your active Python environment.
Import FastAPI from fastapi and assign app = FastAPI() before adding route decorators.
Decorate def root(): with @app.get("/") and return {"Hello": "World"}.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to install uvicorn alongside fastapi.
Naming the app variable something other than app without matching it when starting uvicorn.
steps.run_command: pip install fastapi && pip install uvicorn

steps.title: Run the server with Uvicorn
steps.instructions: Start the server with uvicorn main:app --reload. Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in your browser to see the JSON response.

targets.caption: Confirm Uvicorn started, then visit http://127.0.0.1:8000

explanations.topic: Purpose of main:app and the --reload flag

hints: Run uvicorn from the same directory that contains main.py.
Use the format <filename>:<app_variable> so the command is uvicorn main:app --reload.
Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in your browser after startup completes.
common_mistakes: Running uvicorn from a parent folder instead of the directory containing main.py.

steps.title: Add POST endpoint to create items
steps.instructions: In main.py, initialize an empty items list and add a POST /items route that appends the item query parameter and returns the list. With uvicorn running, test it from a second terminal using curl.

targets.caption: Add the POST /items endpoint below the root route

explanations.topic: How FastAPI routes work and query parameter input

hints: Declare items = [] at module level above your route functions.
Use @app.post("/items") with def create_item(item: str): to accept an item query parameter.
Open a new terminal tab so uvicorn stays running, then send the POST request with curl.
common_mistakes: Stopping the uvicorn server to run curl in the same terminal.
Returning item instead of items and expecting the full list back.

steps.title: Add GET endpoint by item ID
steps.instructions: In main.py, create a GET /items/{item_id} route that reads item_id as an int path parameter and returns the item at that index. Re-populate items via POST, then fetch one by index with curl.

targets.caption: Add the path-parameter GET endpoint for a single item

explanations.topic: Server reload resets in-memory items list
Automatic type conversion from path parameter type hint

hints: Match the variable name inside {item_id} with the function parameter item_id: int.
Remember that saving main.py triggers uvicorn --reload and clears the in-memory items list.
Send a POST request to add at least one item before running curl -X GET http://127.0.0.1:8000/items/0.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to re-add items after uvicorn reloads on file save, causing an IndexError.
Omitting the : int type hint on item_id so it stays a string.

steps.title: Handle missing items with HTTPException
steps.instructions: Import HTTPException in main.py and raise a 404 when item_id is out of range. Then curl an out-of-range ID.

targets.caption: Raise a 404 HTTPException for missing items

explanations.topic: Why HTTP 404 is used instead of 500 Internal Server Error

hints: Add HTTPException to your import line at the top of main.py.
Use if item_id < len(items): to guard indexing into items.
In the else branch, raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Item {item_id} not found").
common_mistakes: Returning HTTPException(...) instead of using the raise keyword.
Using <= len(items) instead of < len(items), which still raises IndexError at the boundary.

steps.title: Add GET endpoint with query limit
steps.instructions: In main.py, add a GET /items route with a limit: int = 10 query parameter that returns items[0:limit]. Test it with curl both with ?limit=3 and without a query parameter.

targets.caption: Add the GET /items endpoint with an optional limit query parameter

explanations.topic: Query parameters with defaults and automatic int conversion

hints: Even though /items already has a POST route, you can also attach @app.get("/items") to it.
Parameters not in the route path become query parameters automatically, and = 10 sets the default.
Return items[0:limit] and test with curl -X GET 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?limit=3'.
common_mistakes: Not quoting the URL in zsh/bash when it contains ? and = characters.
Forgetting to add items via POST after the server reloads before testing GET /items.

steps.title: Define Pydantic Item model for requests
steps.instructions: Import BaseModel from pydantic and define an Item model with text: str and is_done: bool = False. Use Item in create_item and get_item, then POST a JSON body with curl.

targets.caption: Define the Item model and use it in the endpoints

explanations.topic: Sending Pydantic model data in the JSON request body
Making fields required by removing default values

hints: Define class Item(BaseModel): above items = [] with text: str and is_done: bool = False.
Change create_item(item: str) to create_item(item: Item) and get_item(...) -> str to -> Item.
With a BaseModel parameter, pass JSON in the body via curl -d '{"text":"apple"}' instead of a query string.
common_mistakes: Continuing to send ?item=apple in the query string, which fails with field required in body.
Leaving text: str = None when you want text to be a required field.

steps.title: Add response models to GET endpoints
steps.instructions: Add response_model=list[Item] to the GET /items decorator and response_model=Item to GET /items/{item_id}. Save main.py.

targets.caption: Add response_model to both GET decorators

explanations.topic: How response_model documents and validates API outputs

hints: Pass response_model= as a keyword argument inside the @app.get(...) decorator.
Use response_model=list[Item] for list_items and response_model=Item for get_item.
common_mistakes: Putting response_model inside the function signature instead of the @app.get decorator.
Using Item instead of list[Item] on the list_items endpoint.

steps.title: Test endpoints in Swagger UI docs
steps.instructions: Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs in your browser to view the Swagger docs. Expand POST /items, click Try it out, enter an item, and Execute to inspect the 200 response.

targets.caption: Expand POST /items and use Try it out -> Execute to test

hints: Append /docs to your local server URL: http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs.
Click on POST /items, then click the Try it out button on the right.
Edit the JSON text field in the Request body and click Execute to see the response.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to keep uvicorn running while browsing /docs.
Leaving invalid JSON syntax (such as trailing commas) in the Swagger request body editor.
